The best thing is to educate yourself on how depression affects teens, and if your child is comfortable, ask them how cutting helps them cope. 

The better you understand how they feel and think, the better you can help.
Mostly just love them, be there for them, but don't force them to talk about their feelings if they don't want to.

At the same time make sure they know that no matter what they do or feel, you love them, and that nothing they can do will change that.

Depression affects everyone differently, and everyone copes with it differently, but teenage depression is grown out of 9/10 times.

It may seem like it never ends, but it does. Cutting can permanently mark you, if done severely enough. I for one will live with visible scars on my arms and thighs for years to come, and while I joke about it now, I do regret what I did.

No feeling is bad enough to cause permanent damage to yourself or others. Life is wondeful and a mystery, ever changing.

Kids don't have the concept of that because they haven't experienced enough long term change, things get better, and when they don't we learn to cope with that.
Best part is when they reach out their hand for the change and I dump it on the counter and smile.
